title: 33.3 A 125-to-170GHz Power-Efficient Phase Shifter in SiGe BiCMOS with Outphasing Gain and Phase Corrections
problem: Sub-THz phased-array transceivers for high-resolution radar and wireless communications require broadband, power-efficient phase shifters spanning 125–170GHz. Traditional phase-shifter architectures struggle with phase accuracy, amplitude imbalance, and power efficiency at such high frequencies in silicon technologies.
motivation: Sub-THz communications enable fiber-like data rates with beamforming; silicon-based phased arrays reduce cost vs. III-V technologies; efficient phase control is critical for beam steering and signal reception.
method: The phase shifter uses outphasing, a technique that splits the signal into two constant-amplitude paths—this allows the device to handle amplitude and phase changes without wasting power in traditional amplifiers. Built-in gain and phase adjustments compensate for manufacturing variations and temperature changes. The design uses SiGe BiCMOS (a silicon-germanium process combining bipolar and CMOS transistors), which can operate reliably at 125–170GHz while keeping multiple components on a single chip.
key_novelty: This design combines outphasing (splitting the signal into two constant-amplitude paths) with automatic gain and phase adjustments to efficiently shift signals at sub-THz frequencies from 125–170GHz.
contributions: Outphasing technique for simultaneous gain and phase control
Integrated gain and phase correction (PVT compensation)
limitations: Abstract does not provide phase accuracy, gain flatness, power consumption, noise figure, insertion loss, die area, or quantitative comparison with other sub-THz phase shifters.
primary_theme: power-efficient outphasing phase shifter for sub-THz phased arrays
